For the first time since the semi-final of Euro 2016, Portugal and Wales clash in their UEFA Nations League (UNL) opener, with the hosts starting their title defence under new management.

Match News and Current Form

Following another World Cup failure, Portugal are under new management as 72-year-old Jorge Jesus takes the helm of a squad that still contains the 42-year-old Cristiano Ronaldo. The Seleção das Quinas can take heart from losing to the eventual champions Spain in the summer and should fancy their chances of bouncing back here, given that they’re the most successful side in UNL history. Winners of this competition in 2019 and 2025, Portugal enter this as big favourites, not only due to their 31-place advantage over the visitors in the FIFA rankings, but also because they’re unbeaten in their last ten home matches (W9, D1).

Since securing promotion back to UNL League A in November 2024, Craig Bellamy’s Wales tenure has soured, with his failure to guide them to this summer’s World Cup followed by heavy speculation linking him with Burnley. Bellamy will be hamstrung here by the absence of several key players as the Dragons look to improve on their dismal previous showing in the top tier of this competition in 2022/23, when they picked up just one point in six fixtures. Their chances appear bleak with Wales winless in their four matches in 2026 (D2, L2), while their only two victories across their last eight away games (D3, L3) came against minnows Liechtenstein and Kazakhstan.

Head-to-Head History

Portugal’s 2-0 win in 2016 was their third from four H2Hs (L1), while this will be just the second-ever competitive meeting between the nations. Wales last visited Portugal in 2000, going down 3-0 in a match that current manager Bellamy started.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Eight of Portugal’s last nine home games saw both teams score.

Portugal had under 3.5 shots on target in four of their last five matches.

Just one of Wales’ last nine away outings was decided by a multiple-goal margin.

Six of Wales’ last seven games featured exactly 12 corners.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Ronaldo boasts 18 goal involvements in just 20 UNL appearances (G15, A3) and is one of three players across either squad remaining from the last H2H in 2016 in which he netted the opener. Lewis Koumas is primed for more responsibility for Wales across the next few weeks after a strong start to the season for Liverpool following his first international goal in June, his fourth successive strike for club or country to come beyond the hour mark.

Portugal look to have no major absentees, while Wales’ long list of absentees includes Joe Rodon , Karl Darlow and talisman Harry Wilson .

Betting Analysis

Portugal should win fairly comfortably here, but recent trends point to a home win with both teams scoring .

Author: Ryan Fisher
